title: S3 object storage
author: Atlas core
description: Put a document into an S3-compatible bucket, read a small one back, ask whether one is there, list what is under a prefix, copy one, delete one, or mint a time-limited URL somebody can open or upload with — through a server-registered access key. The operation, the bucket and the key are authored in the model; the credential lives on the server, resolved from the vault (ADR-draft-s3-object-store-worker). The two link operations are what makes this reach documents at their real size: they compute a signature and make no call, so the bytes go straight between the store and whoever opens them. A read into a process variable is bounded at 1 MiB and refuses rather than truncates. Works against AWS S3 and against MinIO, Ceph, Garage, Cloudflare R2 or Wasabi — the Worker's endpoint decides which.

properties.label: Worker
properties.description: Name of the configured S3 Worker (Console → Workers), never a key. The attribute behind this field is spelled connector for compatibility with models already deployed.

properties.label: Bucket
properties.description: The bucket this task acts in — one name, never a path. A value with a slash or a colon in it is refused, because it would address a different bucket or a different host.

properties.label: Key (everything but List objects)
properties.description: The object's whole path inside the bucket, without a leading slash. Often a FEEL expression built from the case, e.g. ="faelle/" + vorgang.nummer + "/antrag.pdf". A retry re-runs the task with the same variables, so a key built from a timestamp writes a second object instead of overwriting the first.

properties.label: Content (Put object)
properties.description: What to store. It travels through a process variable, so it is capped at 1 MiB — for anything larger use Link to upload and let the browser that has the document send it straight to the store.

properties.label: Content is (Put/Read object)

choices.name: Text — the characters as they are
Base64 — decode before storing, encode when reading

properties.description: Text is right for JSON, CSV, XML and a letter. Base64 is what a binary needs to survive a process variable at all, and what a form's uploaded file already is.

properties.label: Content type (Put object / Link to upload)
properties.description: What the bytes are, e.g. application/pdf. On Link to upload it is bound into the URL, so whoever uploads must send exactly this type — which is what stops a link minted for a PDF being used to store something else.

properties.label: Prefix (List objects)
properties.description: Only keys that start with this are listed, which is what searching an object store means — S3 has no query language.

properties.label: Delimiter (List objects)
properties.description: Optional. Keys sharing a segment are rolled up into common prefixes instead of listed one by one, so "/" makes a listing read like a folder. They come back in the result's prefixes.

properties.label: Start after (List objects)
properties.description: Optional. Resumes after this key, exclusive. A truncated page answers with nextStartAfter, so passing it back here pages a prefix forward without re-reading what you already have.

properties.label: Maximum keys (List objects)
properties.description: Caps what may land in the result variable. Empty uses 1000, which is also the most the store returns in one call; a larger value is refused at deploy rather than silently answered with 1000.

properties.label: From bucket (Copy object)
properties.description: The bucket the object is copied from. The copy happens inside the store, so the bytes never pass through Atlas.

properties.label: From key (Copy object)
properties.description: The key the object is copied from — often the key an earlier List objects found.

properties.label: Valid for, seconds (the two links)
properties.description: How long the link works. Empty uses one hour; seven days is the most the signature allows. Keep it short: the URL is a key to that one object for anyone who has it, and it is stored in the instance's variables like any other value.

properties.label: Result variable (everything but Delete object)
properties.description: Receives what the store returned. A listing answers with objects, prefixes, truncated and nextStartAfter; a read with content, contentType and size; a check with exists; a link with url and expiresAt. FEEL lists are 1-based, so the first key is =seite.objects[1].key. Delete answers with nothing a process needs, and the compiler refuses a result variable on it.
